**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement contains no take-or-pay exposure for us:

- **Array bears the supply obligation, not us.** §9.1(a) (p0495) and §9.4(b)(i) (p0510) require Array to supply *our* requirements; §9.3(a) (p0501) has Array procure clinical Materials "as reasonably requested in writing by Ono" at cost.
- **Our side holds rights, not obligations.** §9.4(a) (p0508) gives us the right "(but not the obligation)" to manufacture or subcontract ourselves, and §9.4(b) (p0509) gives us the *right* — not a duty — to obtain commercial requirements from Array.
- **No minimum/volume language anywhere.** Searches for minimum, take-or-pay, commit-to-purchase and binding-forecast terms returned nothing; the sole "shortfall" hit (p0430) is a fourth-quarter royalty-rate reconciliation true-up, not a purchase minimum.
- **Noted for follow-up (not a deviation):** forecasting and ordering mechanics are deferred to the future clinical and commercial Supply Agreements, so we should ensure those documents likewise avoid non-cancellable minimums when negotiated.

This sits at the preferred position, so no edit is required.
